pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: Dark brown regions exhibit sharply defined, rectilinear and polygonal geometries. The edges show high-contrast pixel gradients with minimal blurring. Patches on the upper neck are larger and more irregular, while flank patches are smaller, more densely packed, and display smoothed vertices.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: A continuous network of light cream interstitial pathways forming a complete topological graph. Junction nodes primarily exhibit trivalent and tetravalent connectivity. Pathway width is narrow and consistent, maintaining structural continuity across the entire visible flank and neck regions.

dorsal_ridge_profile.edge_serration: The mane along the dorsal neck displays a short, dark, bristly silhouette. It presents a high-frequency, low-amplitude serrated profile with individual hair tufts visible against the background.

other_distinctive_markers: Presence of two avian symbionts (oxpeckers) clinging to the pelage: one positioned on the lower neck/shoulder fold and one on the posterior flank near the tail base.
